newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $63, thin - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade $63, thin - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trading Thursday was light at unchanged levels as packer buyers and cattle owners settled into a standoff, feedlot sources said.

About 1,500 head sold in Kansas at $63.00 per cwt, steady with this week's sales but down $1.00 from a week ago, USDA said. Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots reported 1,200 head sold at $63.00.
Further packer bids at $63.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, the sources said.
Owner resistance to the packer bids increased as prices came close to estimated break-even prices, sources said.

Break-even prices for cattle owners were projected from $61.00 to $63.00, depending on when cattle were placed on feed, to what extent cattle were set back by this winter's harsh weather and by feed costs, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds.

A winter storm was producing wet snow of varying amounts in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas, feedlot sources said. However, the storm was not expected to excessively stress cattle because it was not accompanied by severe cold, they said.
